messages:
clare (PM): quick decision thread: pick final fallback behavior for reserved pools before we cut the sprint. options: proportional token-burn, grace-window (short tokens), or hard-preempt opt-in. need thumbs.

jia (Eng): proportional token-burn = simplest runtime; O(1) checks in hot path. grace-window adds state and timers, more complexity. hard-preempt requires eviction plumbing + legal.

marco (SRE): ops perspective: grace-window gives clearer signals for alerts (start/end). proportional is predictable but can be surprising to customers during long contests. hard-preempt will increase pages. prefer grace-window with short default (60s).

lucy (Sales): customers prefer explicit behavior. they'd pay for hard-preempt guarantees, but for GA we should do grace-window + paid prewarm. include clear console notifications on evictions.

clare (PM): proposal: ship MVP with grace-window = 60s default + proportional fallback after window expires; premium customers can enable hard-preempt behind contract opt-in. docs + SLA will reflect that.

jia (Eng): doable. will implement grace-window timers in runtime + emit events: burst_start, burst_end, preempted. owners: @jia by 2026-08-01.

marco (SRE): I'll add alert rule: contested_pool > 30s -> page, and include automated reclaim steps. owner: @marco by 2026-08-03.

lucy (Sales): I'll prepare customer comms and pricing for paid prewarm/hard-preempt. owner: @lucy by 2026-08-05.

docsbot: Doc stub created: /docs/dedicated/fallback-grace-window.md (draft).

clare (PM): launch gates to add: runtime microbench O(1), canary 48h with staging replay (p95 delta <12%), console shows grace-window timeline + invoice preview. everyone ok?

jia (Eng): :thumbsup:

marco (SRE): :thumbsup:

lucy (Sales): :thumbsup: (flag: one enterprise will request earlier hard-preempt beta)
